result.title: Harnessing Vision-Language Models for Federated Unsupervised Visual Recognition
result.summary: Federated learning (FL) is a promising research paradigm that enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without data sharing. To handle unlabeled data in local clients, existing unsupervised FL research has primarily focused on tasks like clustering and self-supervised representation learning, leaving the critical problem of unsupervised visual recognition largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we introduce FedUR, the first framework designed for unsupervised recognition by leveraging the zero-shot capabilities of pre-trained vision-language models like CLIP. Specifically, FedUR addresses data heterogeneity through a pseudo-labeling mechanism with a class-aware data selection strategy. This strategy first estimates a global pseudo-label distribution, then allocates pseudo-labeled data to clients accordingly. To handle the uncertainty of conventional positive pseudo-labels, FedUR further incorporates class weights and a negative pseudo-labeling strategy. Furthermore, FedUR proposes a personalized prompt aggregation protocol where general visual prompts are aggregated on the server, and personalized text prompts encoding local knowledge are retained on clients. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedUR consistently outperforms baseline methods under both label-level and feature-level distribution shifts. We believe this work paves the way for further advances in federated unsupervised recognition. Code will be available at {github.com/tim-learn/FedUR/}}.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 FedUR，在联邦学习中利用 CLIP 的零样本能力做无监督视觉识别，通过类感知伪标签分配、类别权重与负伪标签缓解数据异构和标签不确定性，并在服务器聚合通用视觉 prompt、客户端保留个性化文本 prompt。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作重心是分布式训练协议与伪标签分配，不涉及推理期 latent 状态生成、视觉证据筛选或停止决策；prompt 的端侧/服务器拆分只是参数聚合策略，与视觉旁路或内部表示保留无具体可核查联系，故排除。
